questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: My host country specializes in my particular field and I wanted to explore new academic opportunities.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I thought it was quite difficult and I felt left alone by the host university.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't receive a lot of assistance. I think due to the fact that my courses were all in Italian, so they aren't used to having Erasmus students, this complicated my first semester and I was very confused about a lot of things.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It's quite difficult to find payable accommodation in Milan, the housing market is quite difficult to enter and there are many accommodations being offered to a prize not affordable for students. 
I found mine first through HousingAnywhere and after that on an Erasmus group on Facebook. I recommend both things, but you need to be lucky - and quick!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's quite difficult to find payable accommodation in Milan, the housing market is quite difficult to enter and there are many accommodations being offered to a prize not affordable for students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Difficult to say, it has nothing to do with the university but more the general housing situation in Milan that's not very accessible.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It's a very liberal registration proces. You can change your registrations throughout the whole semester.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I got helped by other Erasmus students in a big WhatsApp group.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: In the end it worked out.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't do it last minute. It is a difficult system, but you'll get it eventually.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Difficult to say because the teaching styles are so different.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: My host institution taught in a completely different manner. All my exams were oral and based highly on memorialization, learning by heart. It seems old fashioned and completely different from the analytical style I'm used to at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Storia Romana
Letteratura Latina 
Storia della Filosofia Antica

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer:
Archeologia della Magna Grecia 
Archeologia e Storia dell'Arte Greca

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Archeologia e Storia dell'Arte Greca was a good course, a good introduction to archeology for someone coming with no knowledge at all. But also this was an exam of learning by heart.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
I was surprised by the housing prices. 
Also I got my phone stolen during my stay, there are many pickpockets in Milan, be aware.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Public transportation is cheaper than in DK. 
Food and drinks are cheaper than in DK. 
Housing is expensive, at the level of Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were many activities organized by ESN, both sports, cultural and just hanging out-events.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to go to those that interest you, it's a great way to meet new people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go for trips around Italy!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy. It's a bit more chaotic and the bureaucracy can be a struggle.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Bureaucracy, in general and in the pace it works.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Food, architecture, the style of going out and using the city.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1 Be patient with the systems 
2 Ask for help even if they tell you there is none to get 
3 Adjust early on to the different teaching style, it helps towards the exams

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't be too hard on yourself if you don't have the energy to go meet new people all the time. Do it in your own pace.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Learning the language
Meeting really good friends

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
Learning the language, following the courses in Italian.

In the beginning it was difficult being alone in a new country. I wish I could've been better at telling myself that it was gonna be alright. That it takes time to build a life in a new country.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
